pass_a_gloss: It is possible to expect also some prophet of the ungodliness, perhaps not one but more, going to speak to us as the Lord's utterance a thing which the Lord did not order, or as a word of wisdom the one foreign to wisdom, so that he may kill us by the word of his mouth. But we, also then, in the sinner standing together opposite us, let us say: but I, as if dumb, was not hearing, and as if speechless, not opening his mouth; and I became as a human not hearing. For fine is the deafening toward the ungodly words, whenever we give up hope of the setting-right of those saying the worse things.
pass_b_english: We may expect also a certain prophet of impiety, perhaps not one but several, who will speak to us, as the Lord's word, what the Lord did not command (Deuteronomy 18:20), or, as a word of wisdom, what is foreign to wisdom, so that he may kill us with the word of his mouth. But even then, when the sinner stands against us (Psalm 39:1), let us say: “But I, like one deaf, did not hear, and like one mute who does not open his mouth; and I became like a man who does not hear” (Psalm 38:13-14). For deafness to impious words is good, whenever we despair of correcting those who say what is worse.

choices.choice: 2026-11-11: retranslated in full from Koetschau (GCS 2, ch. VIII); the old English was a digest; the old entry under this id was attached to the wrong chapter and did not carry this chapter's false prophets and Psalm 38 deafness.

Checked against the Patristic Text Archive digitisation of Koetschau (pta0007.pta007.pta-grc1), which reads τινὰ προφήτην; rendered “a [certain] prophet”, the bracket marking that the word is read from the digitisation, not the OCR.
Read ἔστι (OCR ἔστε), ὡς σοφίας λόγον (OCR αἷς), ὡσεὶ κωφός (OCR ασεὶ), ἐπανόρθωσιν; λαλήσοντας with MS M (Koetschau's text).
τινὰ is the printed word (OCR τα ἃ), so "certain" is translation, not a supplement; brackets removed.
